name: OWASP Top 10 Proactive Controls
source_notes: Verified against the official OWASP/www-project-proactive-controls GitHub repo, docs/the-top-10/ (cloned 2026-10-05).
caveats: Publication date beyond the year 2024 (and copyright 2024) is not confirmed.
Maturity "lab" comes from the OWASP projects data (level 3); the numeric-to-label mapping for level 3 is inferred.

Each control's Implementation and "Vulnerabilities Prevented" sections were not extracted, so prevention bullets are reinhardt inferences drawn from related Top 10:2025 and cheat-sheet guidance in the notes, and no CWEs are attributed.
C3 and C8 summaries draw partly on content beyond the first Description sentence, which was only partly extracted.
C10 Stop Server Side Request Forgery is new compared with the 2018 edition. Related links to the Top 10 are reinhardt's mapping, not OWASP's.

items.name: Implement Access Control
items.summary: Allow or deny each subject's request to access an object according to a defined policy.
prevention: (inferred) Deny by default and enforce checks on every request in trusted server-side code.
(inferred) Enforce record ownership rather than trusting client-supplied IDs.
(inferred) Never rely on client-side checks as the deciding control.

static: Handlers with data access and no authorization check
Supabase tables without RLS; open Firebase rules
Role checks only in UI components

items.name: Use Cryptography to Protect Data
items.summary: Give extra protection to sensitive data such as passwords, card numbers, health records, PII and secrets, especially data under GDPR or PCI DSS, both at rest and in transit.
prevention: (inferred) Encrypt sensitive data at rest and use TLS in transit.
(inferred) Hash passwords with a slow, salted algorithm such as Argon2id.
(inferred) Keep keys in a KMS/HSM and use a CSPRNG for security values.

items.name: Validate all Input & Handle Exceptions
items.summary: Let only properly formatted data enter software components, encode output for client-side contexts, and handle exceptions safely.
prevention: (inferred) Validate input with allowlists on the server using a schema validator.
(inferred) Use parameterized queries and context-aware output encoding.
(inferred) Handle errors centrally, fail closed and return generic messages.

static: Empty catch blocks and err.stack in responses

items.name: Address Security from the Start
items.summary: Design a secure architecture up front so vulnerabilities are prevented from entering the application.
prevention: (inferred) Threat-model key flows such as authentication, access control and business logic.
(inferred) Reuse secure design patterns and paved-road components.
(inferred) Write security requirements into user stories and test misuse cases.

static: Missing rate limits on sensitive flows

items.name: Secure By Default Configurations
items.summary: Products should resist common exploitation out of the box, with the most secure settings as the defaults.
prevention: (inferred) Harden configurations repeatably and remove unused features.
(inferred) Send security headers and avoid verbose errors.
(inferred) Prefer short-lived credentials over static secrets in config.

static: Debug flags or source maps in production

items.name: Keep your Components Secure
items.summary: Use secure libraries and frameworks with built-in security, and keep third-party components safe and up to date.
prevention: (inferred) Maintain an SBOM and monitor dependencies with SCA.
(inferred) Commit and enforce lockfiles and pin versions deliberately.
(inferred) Replace unmaintained components.

items.name: Secure Digital Identities
items.summary: Handle digital identities, authentication and sessions robustly, verifying that subjects are who they claim to be.
prevention: (inferred) Offer MFA and enforce sound password policy.
(inferred) Rotate session IDs on login and invalidate on logout.
(inferred) Throttle authentication attempts.

items.name: Leverage Browser Security Features
items.summary: Use browser-side policies and mechanisms such as security headers and cookie attributes to protect users.
prevention: (inferred) Deploy a strict nonce- or hash-based CSP.
(inferred) Set HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and frame-ancestors.
(inferred) Use Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite cookie attributes.

items.name: Implement Security Logging and Monitoring
items.summary: Log security-relevant information at runtime and monitor it to detect and respond to attacks.
prevention: (inferred) Log authentication, authorization and validation failures with context.
(inferred) Never log secrets, tokens or sensitive PII; encode log data.
(inferred) Alert on suspicious activity.

static: No logging in auth failure paths

items.name: Stop Server Side Request Forgery
items.summary: Prevent the server from being tricked into making unintended requests to internal or external services.
prevention: (inferred) Allowlist destination hosts, schemes and ports.
(inferred) Disable redirect following and validate resolved IPs.
(inferred) Block private and metadata addresses and segment the network.
